# OBJECTION HANDLING GUIDE

Use the L.E.A.D. framework before answering any objection: Listen, Establish belief, Amplify certainty, then Diagnose the real concern. Do not rush into defending the offer. Clarify what is actually holding them back, then use the most relevant response below.

**OBJECTION: "Why is the initial engagement 90 days?"**

Our first 90 days together are intentionally designed as an intensive growth phase. Most med spa owners come to us because they want more clients and more qualified leads, so our goal is to get the right acquisition strategy moving quickly and begin creating measurable momentum within the first 30 days.

But sustainable growth requires more than simply turning on ads. During those 90 days, we dig deep into your med spa, identify the biggest revenue leaks and growth opportunities, build your Growth Blueprint, implement the highest impact strategies and systems, and optimize based on real data. That initial phase requires significantly more strategy, implementation, and hands-on support, which is why it is structured as an upfront 90-day investment.

After that foundation is built, our goal is not to disappear. We transition into a long-term growth partnership where we continue optimizing, evolving, and scaling what we have built together as your med spa grows. We also intentionally do not lock you into the year-long contracts that are common with many agencies. We believe we need to earn your trust first, and that matters to us. The initial 90 days give us the opportunity to show you how we work, create momentum, and build the foundation for a long-term partnership because you want to continue growing with us, not because you are stuck in a contract.

**OBJECTION: "So are you a marketing agency or a consulting company?"**

We are a med spa growth company. Marketing is an important part of growth, but we do not assume every med spa needs the same marketing strategy or that more leads are always the only answer.

We look at the practice, the market, and where the biggest growth opportunities and revenue leaks are first. Then we determine what needs to be strengthened internally using our proven Growth Playbooks and what acquisition strategy makes the most sense externally. Our job is not to sell you a specific marketing channel or hand you advice and leave you to figure it out. It is to identify what is most likely to move your business forward and help implement it in the right order.

**OBJECTION: "What kind of marketing will you run for us?"**

That depends on what the data tells us. We do not force every med spa into the same channel or automatically prescribe Meta, Google, SEO, GEO, organic, reactivation, or any single strategy just because it is something we can provide.

We look at your market, competition, patient behavior, existing visibility, current marketing, and internal systems first. From there, we determine the acquisition strategy that makes the most sense for your specific med spa. For some practices, that may mean leaning heavily into one channel. For others, it may be a strategic combination. We diagnose first, then prescribe the strategy.

**OBJECTION: "How quickly should I expect to see results? Will I see results in the first 30 days?"**

Our goal is to create measurable momentum within the first 30 days, especially on the patient acquisition side. We also have proven methods to activate your current client base and uncover opportunities already sitting inside your practice, which can create quick wins while we amplify the rest of the growth plan and put the larger strategy into place. Many of the acquisition strategies we implement are designed to begin generating activity quickly, but we also want to be clear that sustainable growth is not about creating a short-term spike in leads.

The full 90-day engagement gives us time to launch, gather real data, optimize what is working, and strengthen the systems that turn new and existing opportunities into actual revenue. We are building for both immediate movement and sustainable long-term growth, so that what works can continue scaling with you beyond the initial 90 days.

**OBJECTION: "It's too expensive." *(updated)***

I completely understand. Let me ask you something so I can understand what you mean by expensive. Is it that the investment is outside of what the business can comfortably do right now, or are you still unsure whether the return would justify the investment?

The reason I ask is because those are two different concerns. If you believe the strategy can help solve the problems we discussed, then the real question is what continuing with those problems is already costing the business.

If the Premium Growth Program is the right fit for you, that path is also backed by our guarantee, 50 paid clients in your first 90 days, or we keep working at no additional cost until we hit it. With the Growth Partnership, you're getting the full diagnostic and the exact system to implement it, at a lower investment, with your team driving execution.

We also understand that cash flow and timing matter. We do have financing options available, and we can split either investment into two payments to make getting started more manageable, two payments of $4,500 for the Growth Partnership, or two payments of $7,500 for the Premium Growth Program.

**OBJECTION: "This isn't the right time."**

I understand. What specifically would need to change for it to become the right time?

The reason I ask is that many of the issues we discussed do not stay neutral while you wait. Missed leads, patients who do not return, weak conversion, inconsistent marketing, and revenue leaks continue costing the practice every month. If there is a legitimate timing issue, we can talk through it. But if the business needs these changes in order to reach the goals you told me are important, waiting for everything to feel perfectly convenient may actually delay the outcome you want.

**OBJECTION: "I need to think about it."**

Absolutely. What specifically do you feel you still need to think through?

Usually when someone says they need to think about it, there is one part of the decision they are not fully comfortable with yet. It could be the investment, timing, trust, implementation, or uncertainty about whether this will work for their practice. I would rather understand what that is and answer it directly than have you leave with an unanswered concern.

**OBJECTION: "I need to talk to my partner / spouse / business partner."**

Of course. Is your partner involved in the business decision, the financial decision, or both?

Based on everything we discussed today, do you personally believe this is the right direction for the practice? If so, let's make sure you have everything you need to have a productive conversation with them. If they are a key decision maker, we can also bring them into a short follow up conversation so they can ask questions directly rather than putting you in the position of having to recreate the entire strategy session for them.

**OBJECTION: "I'm shopping around / talking to other agencies."**

That makes sense. You should feel confident in whoever you choose. As you compare options, I would encourage you to look beyond the list of deliverables and ask how each company determines what your med spa actually needs before they start spending your money.

Our difference is that we are not walking in with one predetermined solution. We diagnose the entire growth ecosystem, look at both the internal revenue opportunities and the external market, and then build the strategy around what the data shows. So I would compare not only who can run ads or provide marketing services, but who is actually looking at the business as a whole and taking responsibility for the larger growth picture.

**OBJECTION: "I'm not sure this will work for my med spa."**

That is a fair concern, especially if you have invested in things before that did not produce the result you expected. What specifically makes you unsure?

One of the reasons we start with the Revenue Leak Audit and Growth Blueprint is because we do not assume the same strategy will work for every practice. We look at your actual business, market, opportunities, and constraints before deciding what to implement. The strategy is built around your med spa rather than forcing your med spa into a generic system.

**OBJECTION: "We've tried marketing agencies before and got burned."**

I understand why you would be cautious. What happened with the previous agency?

That experience is exactly why our process starts differently. We do not begin by immediately prescribing the service we happen to sell. We look at what happened before, what your market actually supports, where your current systems may be losing opportunities, and what needs to be different this time. We also do not lock you into a year-long contract. We believe trust should be earned through the work and the results.

**OBJECTION: "We already have a marketing agency."**

That may be completely fine. We are not automatically assuming your current agency needs to be replaced. The question is whether the current strategy is producing the growth you want and whether anyone is looking beyond lead generation at the entire revenue ecosystem.

Depending on what we uncover, the answer may be improving what is already in place, filling gaps your current agency is not addressing, or changing the acquisition strategy altogether. We want to diagnose the opportunity first rather than make assumptions.

**OBJECTION: "We already get plenty of leads."**

That is actually an important distinction, because more leads may not be where your biggest opportunity is. If you already have strong lead volume, we would want to understand how quickly those leads are contacted, how many book, how many show, how many convert, and what happens after the first treatment.

Sometimes the fastest path to growth is not buying more traffic. It is converting more of the opportunities you already paid for and increasing the lifetime value of the patients already inside the practice.

**OBJECTION: "We don't have enough leads. I just want marketing."**

And patient acquisition may absolutely be a major part of the solution. We are not against turning on marketing quickly. What we do not want to do is spend your money blindly.

We first determine which channels make the most sense for your market and make sure the basic systems are in place to respond to and convert the demand we create. That allows us to pursue more leads while also making sure more of those leads have a real chance of becoming revenue.

**OBJECTION: "Can't we just start with ads and fix everything else later?"**

We can move quickly on acquisition when the data supports it, but we do not want to create demand faster than the practice can capture it. If leads are not being contacted quickly, consultations are not converting, or follow up is inconsistent, increasing ad spend can simply increase the amount of money being lost.

The goal is not to delay marketing. It is to make sure the acquisition strategy and the systems behind it are working together so the money you spend has a better chance of producing an actual return.

**OBJECTION: "Can we start with something smaller or cheaper?"**

Possibly, but I would not recommend reducing the solution to the point that it no longer solves the problem we identified. Based on what you shared, the growth constraints are connected. Addressing only one small piece may feel less expensive upfront, but it can also leave the larger issue unchanged.

The better question is whether there is a way to structure the engagement responsibly without compromising the strategy. If there is, we can discuss it. But I would not want to sell you a smaller solution simply to make the sale if I do not believe it will get you where you want to go.

**OBJECTION: "I don't have the bandwidth or staff to implement this."**

That is exactly why we need to understand the level of implementation support you need. The goal is not to hand you another binder of ideas or create more work that sits on your desk.

We identify the highest impact priorities, put them in the right order, and support the implementation based on the engagement you choose. Part of building a scalable med spa is reducing the number of things that depend entirely on the owner.

**OBJECTION: "My team won't follow through."**

That is a real concern, and it is also often part of the growth problem itself. A strategy only works if the team can actually execute it.

That is why we look at systems, accountability, KPIs, workflows, and team adoption rather than simply giving you recommendations. If team follow through is a known bottleneck, that becomes part of what we need to address in the growth plan.

**OBJECTION: "I need to wait until we hire another provider / injector."**

That may be the right operational decision, but I would want to understand whether waiting truly needs to stop all growth work. There may be things we can strengthen now, such as reactivation, retention, conversion, systems, positioning, or building the acquisition foundation, so you are not starting from zero once the new provider arrives.

The question is whether we should pause everything or use this time to make sure the practice is ready to capitalize on the added capacity.

**OBJECTION: "I want to see a proposal first."**

Absolutely. We can make sure the scope and investment are clear. I would just want to make sure we do not reduce this decision to comparing a checklist of deliverables.

The strategy should reflect what we uncovered about your practice and what we believe needs to happen to reach the goal you described. I am happy to walk through the recommendation with you so you understand not only what is included, but why those priorities were chosen.

**OBJECTION: "Can you guarantee how many leads or new patients I'll get?" *(updated)***

That depends on which path makes sense for your practice.

With the Growth Partnership, your team is running implementation, so it wouldn't be responsible for us to promise a specific number we don't control. What we do guarantee is that the Revenue Leak Audit and Blueprint will show you exactly what to fix and where your real opportunity is, not a guess.

With the Premium Growth Program, we're the ones running your ads and actively involved in implementation, so we can and do guarantee 50 paid, closed clients within your first 90 days, drawing from both new patient acquisition and reactivation of your existing database. If we don't hit it, we keep working at no additional cost until we do.

**OBJECTION: "What happens after the 90 days?" *(updated)***

We don't disappear at the end of the 90 days. For Premium Growth Program clients, we transition into an ongoing partnership: we continue running your marketing for $3,000 a month, you get direct access to our team through Slack for ongoing questions and support, and you have the option to book a call directly with me anytime you want to talk through the next stage of growth.

We don't lock you into a year-long contract for that ongoing partnership. You've already seen what we can do during the initial 90 days, so continuing together is your call to make, not something you're stuck doing.

**OBJECTION: "I need to wait until cash flow improves."**

I understand. Is the cash flow issue temporary, or is inconsistent revenue one of the reasons you are considering getting help in the first place?

If the business genuinely cannot support the investment, that is important to acknowledge. But if the same revenue leaks and growth constraints we discussed are contributing to the cash flow problem, waiting for the problem to fix itself may not change the situation. We should look at the numbers realistically and decide whether solving the underlying issue now makes sense.

**OBJECTION: "Send me some information and I'll get back to you."**

Absolutely, I can send information. Before we end, though, what specifically would you want to review in order to make a decision?

I ask because sending a generic deck usually does not answer the real question someone has. If there is something you are uncertain about, I would rather make sure I send you exactly what is relevant and agree on a clear next step rather than leaving the conversation open ended.

**STEP 1: Diagnose the Growth Opportunity**

Before we change your marketing, turn on ads, or start implementing new systems, we need to know exactly where the greatest opportunities and leaks are.

We start with our Revenue Leak Audit and extensive Market Growth Blueprint. We look at the business from both directions.

# OBJECTION HANDLING GUIDE

Use the L.E.A.D. framework before answering any objection: Listen, Establish belief, Amplify certainty, then Diagnose the real concern. Do not rush into defending the offer. Clarify what is actually holding them back, then use the most relevant response below.

**OBJECTION: "Why is the initial engagement 90 days?"**

Our first 90 days together are intentionally designed as an intensive growth phase. Most med spa owners come to us because they want more clients and more qualified leads, so our goal is to get the right acquisition strategy moving quickly and begin creating measurable momentum within the first 30 days.

But sustainable growth requires more than simply turning on ads. During those 90 days, we dig deep into your med spa, identify the biggest revenue leaks and growth opportunities, build your Growth Blueprint, implement the highest impact strategies and systems, and optimize based on real data. That initial phase requires significantly more strategy, implementation, and hands-on support, which is why it is structured as an upfront 90-day investment.

After that foundation is built, our goal is not to disappear. We transition into a long-term growth partnership where we continue optimizing, evolving, and scaling what we have built together as your med spa grows. We also intentionally do not lock you into the year-long contracts that are common with many agencies. We believe we need to earn your trust first, and that matters to us. The initial 90 days give us the opportunity to show you how we work, create momentum, and build the foundation for a long-term partnership because you want to continue growing with us, not because you are stuck in a contract.

**OBJECTION: "So are you a marketing agency or a consulting company?"**

We are a med spa growth company. Marketing is an important part of growth, but we do not assume every med spa needs the same marketing strategy or that more leads are always the only answer.

We look at the practice, the market, and where the biggest growth opportunities and revenue leaks are first. Then we determine what needs to be strengthened internally using our proven Growth Playbooks and what acquisition strategy makes the most sense externally. Our job is not to sell you a specific marketing channel or hand you advice and leave you to figure it out. It is to identify what is most likely to move your business forward and help implement it in the right order.

**OBJECTION: "What kind of marketing will you run for us?"**

That depends on what the data tells us. We do not force every med spa into the same channel or automatically prescribe Meta, Google, SEO, GEO, organic, reactivation, or any single strategy just because it is something we can provide.

We look at your market, competition, patient behavior, existing visibility, current marketing, and internal systems first. From there, we determine the acquisition strategy that makes the most sense for your specific med spa. For some practices, that may mean leaning heavily into one channel. For others, it may be a strategic combination. We diagnose first, then prescribe the strategy.

**OBJECTION: "How quickly should I expect to see results? Will I see results in the first 30 days?"**

Our goal is to create measurable momentum within the first 30 days, especially on the patient acquisition side. We also have proven methods to activate your current client base and uncover opportunities already sitting inside your practice, which can create quick wins while we amplify the rest of the growth plan and put the larger strategy into place. Many of the acquisition strategies we implement are designed to begin generating activity quickly, but we also want to be clear that sustainable growth is not about creating a short-term spike in leads.

The full 90-day engagement gives us time to launch, gather real data, optimize what is working, and strengthen the systems that turn new and existing opportunities into actual revenue. We are building for both immediate movement and sustainable long-term growth, so that what works can continue scaling with you beyond the initial 90 days.

**OBJECTION: "It's too expensive." *(updated)***

I completely understand. Let me ask you something so I can understand what you mean by expensive. Is it that the investment is outside of what the business can comfortably do right now, or are you still unsure whether the return would justify the investment?

The reason I ask is because those are two different concerns. If you believe the strategy can help solve the problems we discussed, then the real question is what continuing with those problems is already costing the business.

If the Premium Growth Program is the right fit for you, that path is also backed by our guarantee, 50 paid clients in your first 90 days, or we keep working at no additional cost until we hit it. With the Growth Partnership, you're getting the full diagnostic and the exact system to implement it, at a lower investment, with your team driving execution.

We also understand that cash flow and timing matter. We do have financing options available, and we can split either investment into two payments to make getting started more manageable, two payments of $4,500 for the Growth Partnership, or two payments of $7,500 for the Premium Growth Program.

**OBJECTION: "This isn't the right time."**

I understand. What specifically would need to change for it to become the right time?

The reason I ask is that many of the issues we discussed do not stay neutral while you wait. Missed leads, patients who do not return, weak conversion, inconsistent marketing, and revenue leaks continue costing the practice every month. If there is a legitimate timing issue, we can talk through it. But if the business needs these changes in order to reach the goals you told me are important, waiting for everything to feel perfectly convenient may actually delay the outcome you want.

**OBJECTION: "I need to think about it."**

Absolutely. What specifically do you feel you still need to think through?

Usually when someone says they need to think about it, there is one part of the decision they are not fully comfortable with yet. It could be the investment, timing, trust, implementation, or uncertainty about whether this will work for their practice. I would rather understand what that is and answer it directly than have you leave with an unanswered concern.

**OBJECTION: "I need to talk to my partner / spouse / business partner."**

Of course. Is your partner involved in the business decision, the financial decision, or both?

Based on everything we discussed today, do you personally believe this is the right direction for the practice? If so, let's make sure you have everything you need to have a productive conversation with them. If they are a key decision maker, we can also bring them into a short follow up conversation so they can ask questions directly rather than putting you in the position of having to recreate the entire strategy session for them.

**OBJECTION: "I'm shopping around / talking to other agencies."**

That makes sense. You should feel confident in whoever you choose. As you compare options, I would encourage you to look beyond the list of deliverables and ask how each company determines what your med spa actually needs before they start spending your money.

Our difference is that we are not walking in with one predetermined solution. We diagnose the entire growth ecosystem, look at both the internal revenue opportunities and the external market, and then build the strategy around what the data shows. So I would compare not only who can run ads or provide marketing services, but who is actually looking at the business as a whole and taking responsibility for the larger growth picture.

**OBJECTION: "I'm not sure this will work for my med spa."**

That is a fair concern, especially if you have invested in things before that did not produce the result you expected. What specifically makes you unsure?

One of the reasons we start with the Revenue Leak Audit and Growth Blueprint is because we do not assume the same strategy will work for every practice. We look at your actual business, market, opportunities, and constraints before deciding what to implement. The strategy is built around your med spa rather than forcing your med spa into a generic system.

**OBJECTION: "We've tried marketing agencies before and got burned."**

I understand why you would be cautious. What happened with the previous agency?

That experience is exactly why our process starts differently. We do not begin by immediately prescribing the service we happen to sell. We look at what happened before, what your market actually supports, where your current systems may be losing opportunities, and what needs to be different this time. We also do not lock you into a year-long contract. We believe trust should be earned through the work and the results.

**OBJECTION: "We already have a marketing agency."**

That may be completely fine. We are not automatically assuming your current agency needs to be replaced. The question is whether the current strategy is producing the growth you want and whether anyone is looking beyond lead generation at the entire revenue ecosystem.

Depending on what we uncover, the answer may be improving what is already in place, filling gaps your current agency is not addressing, or changing the acquisition strategy altogether. We want to diagnose the opportunity first rather than make assumptions.

**OBJECTION: "We already get plenty of leads."**

That is actually an important distinction, because more leads may not be where your biggest opportunity is. If you already have strong lead volume, we would want to understand how quickly those leads are contacted, how many book, how many show, how many convert, and what happens after the first treatment.

Sometimes the fastest path to growth is not buying more traffic. It is converting more of the opportunities you already paid for and increasing the lifetime value of the patients already inside the practice.

**OBJECTION: "We don't have enough leads. I just want marketing."**

And patient acquisition may absolutely be a major part of the solution. We are not against turning on marketing quickly. What we do not want to do is spend your money blindly.

We first determine which channels make the most sense for your market and make sure the basic systems are in place to respond to and convert the demand we create. That allows us to pursue more leads while also making sure more of those leads have a real chance of becoming revenue.

**OBJECTION: "Can't we just start with ads and fix everything else later?"**

We can move quickly on acquisition when the data supports it, but we do not want to create demand faster than the practice can capture it. If leads are not being contacted quickly, consultations are not converting, or follow up is inconsistent, increasing ad spend can simply increase the amount of money being lost.

The goal is not to delay marketing. It is to make sure the acquisition strategy and the systems behind it are working together so the money you spend has a better chance of producing an actual return.

**OBJECTION: "Can we start with something smaller or cheaper?"**

Possibly, but I would not recommend reducing the solution to the point that it no longer solves the problem we identified. Based on what you shared, the growth constraints are connected. Addressing only one small piece may feel less expensive upfront, but it can also leave the larger issue unchanged.

The better question is whether there is a way to structure the engagement responsibly without compromising the strategy. If there is, we can discuss it. But I would not want to sell you a smaller solution simply to make the sale if I do not believe it will get you where you want to go.

**OBJECTION: "I don't have the bandwidth or staff to implement this."**

That is exactly why we need to understand the level of implementation support you need. The goal is not to hand you another binder of ideas or create more work that sits on your desk.

We identify the highest impact priorities, put them in the right order, and support the implementation based on the engagement you choose. Part of building a scalable med spa is reducing the number of things that depend entirely on the owner.

**OBJECTION: "My team won't follow through."**

That is a real concern, and it is also often part of the growth problem itself. A strategy only works if the team can actually execute it.

That is why we look at systems, accountability, KPIs, workflows, and team adoption rather than simply giving you recommendations. If team follow through is a known bottleneck, that becomes part of what we need to address in the growth plan.

**OBJECTION: "I need to wait until we hire another provider / injector."**

That may be the right operational decision, but I would want to understand whether waiting truly needs to stop all growth work. There may be things we can strengthen now, such as reactivation, retention, conversion, systems, positioning, or building the acquisition foundation, so you are not starting from zero once the new provider arrives.

The question is whether we should pause everything or use this time to make sure the practice is ready to capitalize on the added capacity.

**OBJECTION: "I want to see a proposal first."**

Absolutely. We can make sure the scope and investment are clear. I would just want to make sure we do not reduce this decision to comparing a checklist of deliverables.

The strategy should reflect what we uncovered about your practice and what we believe needs to happen to reach the goal you described. I am happy to walk through the recommendation with you so you understand not only what is included, but why those priorities were chosen.

**OBJECTION: "Can you guarantee how many leads or new patients I'll get?" *(updated)***

That depends on which path makes sense for your practice.

With the Growth Partnership, your team is running implementation, so it wouldn't be responsible for us to promise a specific number we don't control. What we do guarantee is that the Revenue Leak Audit and Blueprint will show you exactly what to fix and where your real opportunity is, not a guess.

With the Premium Growth Program, we're the ones running your ads and actively involved in implementation, so we can and do guarantee 50 paid, closed clients within your first 90 days, drawing from both new patient acquisition and reactivation of your existing database. If we don't hit it, we keep working at no additional cost until we do.

**OBJECTION: "What happens after the 90 days?" *(updated)***

We don't disappear at the end of the 90 days. For Premium Growth Program clients, we transition into an ongoing partnership: we continue running your marketing for $3,000 a month, you get direct access to our team through Slack for ongoing questions and support, and you have the option to book a call directly with me anytime you want to talk through the next stage of growth.

We don't lock you into a year-long contract for that ongoing partnership. You've already seen what we can do during the initial 90 days, so continuing together is your call to make, not something you're stuck doing.

**OBJECTION: "I need to wait until cash flow improves."**

I understand. Is the cash flow issue temporary, or is inconsistent revenue one of the reasons you are considering getting help in the first place?

If the business genuinely cannot support the investment, that is important to acknowledge. But if the same revenue leaks and growth constraints we discussed are contributing to the cash flow problem, waiting for the problem to fix itself may not change the situation. We should look at the numbers realistically and decide whether solving the underlying issue now makes sense.

**OBJECTION: "Send me some information and I'll get back to you."**

Absolutely, I can send information. Before we end, though, what specifically would you want to review in order to make a decision?

I ask because sending a generic deck usually does not answer the real question someone has. If there is something you are uncertain about, I would rather make sure I send you exactly what is relevant and agree on a clear next step rather than leaving the conversation open ended.

# TLC Call Scripts: Before / After Comparison

---

## QUICK SUMMARY

| Section | What Changed |
|---|---|
| Offer | DWY / DFY renamed to Growth Partnership / Premium Growth Program, redefined by scope of service instead of who implements |
| Guarantee | 2X revenue guarantee replaced with 50 paid clients in 90 days, tied to a Market Blueprint spend contingency, applies to Premium tier only |
| Close | Added an optional guarantee reinforcement line for Premium-leaning prospects |
| Objection: "It's too expensive" | Guarantee reference updated, payment split numbers corrected to match actual pricing |
| Objection: "Can you guarantee how many leads or patients I'll get?" | Fully rewritten to answer per tier instead of arguing against giving any number |
| Objection: "What happens after the 90 days?" | Vague "ongoing partnership" language replaced with specific $3,000/month, Slack access, and calls with Bethany |

---

## OFFER

**BEFORE**
> Option 1
> Done With You Med Spa Growth Accelerator
> Investment: $9,000
> We'll work directly with you and your team to guide the implementation of every stage of the growth system.
>
> Option 2
> Done For You Med Spa Growth Accelerator
> Investment: $15,000
> Our team handles implementation for you including marketing systems, patient journey optimization, automation, operations and reporting. Everything. This is designed for owners who want faster implementation while minimizing internal workload.

**AFTER**
> Option 1: Growth Partnership
> Investment: $9,000
> We complete your Revenue Leak Audit and Market Blueprint, then hand you the exact playbooks and course content to implement every stage of the growth system with your own team.
>
> Option 2: Premium Growth Program
> Investment: $15,000
> Same Revenue Leak Audit and Market Blueprint. We run your ads, and we hold bi-weekly implementation calls to build the playbooks, course systems, and major retention infrastructure together, so it actually gets built, not just handed to you.

**Why it changed:** the old naming was internal agency jargon that didn't communicate anything to a prospect. The new version defines each tier by what's actually delivered, and sets up why the guarantee can only live in the top tier (TLC controls execution there).

---

## GUARANTEE

**BEFORE**
> To remove as much risk as possible, if we don't help you generate at least 2X your investment in new or recovered revenue during our engagement, we'll continue working with you at no additional cost until we do.

**AFTER**
> **If they choose the Premium Growth Program:**
> "Since we're the ones running your ads and actively involved in implementation, we can back this with a real number. We guarantee 50 paid, closed clients within your first 90 days, through a combination of new patient acquisition and reactivation of your existing patient database. If we don't hit that number, we keep working at no additional cost until we do, as long as the contingencies below are being met on your end."
>
> **Contingencies:**
> - Minimum ad spend maintained as outlined in the practice's Market Blueprint
> - Existing patient database of sufficient size and quality to support reactivation
> - Minimum patient and provider capacity to absorb 50 new clients across 90 days
> - CRM adopted and used as system of record from day one
> - Speed to Lead automation active before ads launch
> - Agreed follow up response time met on every lead
> - Staff complete TLC's sales training within an agreed window
> - Bi-weekly implementation calls attended
> - No pausing ads, changing offers, or running conflicting campaigns without coordinating with TLC
> - Guarantee based on figures the client provides at onboarding; materially misrepresented figures void it
> - Onboarding and account access completed within an agreed window
> - Guarantee clock can pause, not void, for events outside TLC's control
>
> **If they choose the Growth Partnership:**
> "Because your team is running implementation on this path, it wouldn't be responsible for us to promise a specific patient number we don't control. What we do guarantee is that your Revenue Leak Audit and Market Blueprint will be built specifically around your practice and your market, not a generic template, and that you'll walk away knowing exactly what to fix and in what order."

**Why it changed:** a revenue guarantee put TLC on the hook for variables the client controls (close rate, staff execution, pricing). A client-count guarantee, tied to real funnel math and protected by specific contingencies, only applies where TLC actually runs the acquisition and co-implements the systems. It also no longer applies to the Growth Partnership tier, since TLC has no execution control there.

---

## CLOSE

**BEFORE**
> Based on everything we've discussed today, which option feels like the better fit for your clinic?

**AFTER**
> Based on everything we've discussed today, which option feels like the better fit for your clinic?
>
> **Optional reinforcement, if the prospect is leaning toward Premium:** "And just so it's clear, if you go with the Premium Growth Program, that's the path backed by our guarantee, we don't stop until we've brought you 50 paid clients in your first 90 days."

**Why it changed:** gives reps an optional line to reinforce the guarantee right before the close, without forcing it into every conversation regardless of which tier the prospect is leaning toward.

---

## OBJECTION: "It's too expensive"

**BEFORE**
> ...Our goal is not to become another expense on your P&L. We are looking for new and recoverable revenue opportunities that can create a measurable return on the investment. That is also why we back the engagement with our 2X guarantee.
>
> We also understand that cash flow and timing matter. We do have financing options available, and we can also split the investment into two payments of $8,000 to make getting started more manageable. And remember, we stand behind the work with our guarantee: if we don't help you generate at least 2X your investment in new or recoverable revenue during our engagement, we'll continue working with you at no additional cost until we do.

**AFTER**
> ...If the Premium Growth Program is the right fit for you, that path is also backed by our guarantee, 50 paid clients in your first 90 days, or we keep working at no additional cost until we hit it. With the Growth Partnership, you're getting the full diagnostic and the exact system to implement it, at a lower investment, with your team driving execution.
>
> We also understand that cash flow and timing matter. We do have financing options available, and we can split either investment into two payments to make getting started more manageable, two payments of $4,500 for the Growth Partnership, or two payments of $7,500 for the Premium Growth Program.

**Why it changed:** the guarantee reference was updated to match the new promise, and the payment split was corrected. The original "$8,000 x 2" totaled $16,000, which didn't match either the $9,000 or $15,000 tier.

---

## OBJECTION: "Can you guarantee how many leads or new patients I'll get?"

**BEFORE**
> We do not believe it is responsible to promise an arbitrary number of leads without first understanding the market, budget, offer, competition, and conversion systems behind the campaign. More leads also do not automatically mean more revenue.
>
> What we can do is build the strategy around real data, optimize aggressively, activate opportunities already inside the practice for quicker wins, and focus on measurable new or recovered revenue. That is why our guarantee is tied to helping generate at least 2X the investment in new or recoverable revenue rather than simply delivering a vanity metric.

**AFTER**
> That depends on which path makes sense for your practice.
>
> With the Growth Partnership, your team is running implementation, so it wouldn't be responsible for us to promise a specific number we don't control. What we do guarantee is that the Revenue Leak Audit and Blueprint will show you exactly what to fix and where your real opportunity is, not a guess.
>
> With the Premium Growth Program, we're the ones running your ads and actively involved in implementation, so we can and do guarantee 50 paid, closed clients within your first 90 days, drawing from both new patient acquisition and reactivation of your existing database. If we don't hit it, we keep working at no additional cost until we do.

**Why it changed:** the old answer argued against ever giving a number at all. That's now inconsistent with the new ads, which lead with a results claim, and with the new guarantee, which does commit to a specific number for the Premium tier. The updated version gives a real, tier-specific answer instead of deflecting.

---

## OBJECTION: "What happens after the 90 days?"

**BEFORE**
> At the end of the initial 90 days, we look at what we have built, what is producing results, and where the next growth opportunities are. The goal is to transition into an ongoing partnership focused on continued optimization and scale.
>
> We do not want you staying because a year-long contract forces you to. We want to earn the opportunity to keep working together because the partnership is creating value and there is a clear path for continued growth.

**AFTER**
> We don't disappear at the end of the 90 days. For Premium Growth Program clients, we transition into an ongoing partnership: we continue running your marketing for $3,000 a month, you get direct access to our team through Slack for ongoing questions and support, and you have the option to book a call directly with me anytime you want to talk through the next stage of growth.
>
> We don't lock you into a year-long contract for that ongoing partnership. You've already seen what we can do during the initial 90 days, so continuing together is your call to make, not something you're stuck doing.

**Why it changed:** the original answer was vague about what "ongoing partnership" actually meant. The update gives a prospect something concrete to picture and price out, which is more reassuring than a generic promise.

---

## UNCHANGED

Everything else in the Triage script, the Demo script's Discovery, Pain & Impact, Current Solutions, Future Pace, and four-stage Pitch, and the remaining 15 objections in the Objection Guide, stayed exactly as originally written. Those sections didn't reference the old guarantee or offer structure, so nothing there needed to move.

# The Luxora Collective: Sharpened Ad Copy
### Course fatigue positioning, with hooks rebuilt for scene-level specificity and loss aversion

---

## WHY THESE HOOKS HIT HARDER

The original hooks ("leads sitting in a spreadsheet," "a course collecting dust") are true but generic, any med spa owner nods along without picturing anything specific. The training's own strongest example never just stated the problem, it walked through an exact scene, so specific the prospect couldn't argue with the conclusion. These versions do the same thing: a specific time of night, a specific dollar figure, a specific number of leads lost today, and the specific competitor who got the patient instead. Specificity is what turns a general nod into "that's literally me."

---

## VIDEO AD SCRIPT, PRIMARY (60 to 90 seconds)

> It's 9pm. You're scrolling through module six of a course you paid three thousand dollars for, because you told yourself you'd build this system eventually. You still haven't opened module two.
>
> Meanwhile, five leads came in today. Two never got a call back before your front desk clocked out. One booked a consult and never showed. By next week, most of them will have already found a med spa that called them back in ten minutes instead of two days.
>
> You don't need more leads sitting in a spreadsheet nobody calls. And you don't need another course collecting dust in a folder you already paid for.
>
> If you're a med spa owner, you've probably tried both. Ads that generated leads no one followed up on fast enough. A course or a consultant who told you exactly what to do, and you never had the three extra hours a week to actually build it.
>
> Here's the truth: the problem was never information. It's that you're running a practice, not a marketing department, and no course was ever going to change that.
>
> That's the gap The Luxora Collective closes.
>
> We run your marketing, so qualified patients are actually showing up. And we hand you the exact playbooks and systems, built from nearly two decades running the back end of practices like yours, so your team knows precisely how to turn those patients into long-term, high-value relationships. Follow-up scripts. Membership and package structures. Staff sales training. Not a binder of theory. A system built to be used.
>
> For qualified med spas, we guarantee [X] new patient opportunities a month, patients scheduled, shown up, and ready to buy. If we don't hit the number, we keep working at no additional fee until we do.
>
> Click below for your Revenue Leak Audit, and we'll show you exactly where your practice is losing patients, and what fixing it is worth.

---

## ALTERNATE HOOKS (swap into the same script for A/B testing, rest of script stays identical)

**Hook Option 2: Identity / ego pain**

> You're a great injector. You built a real practice, from nothing, with your own hands. And somehow you're still doing sales, marketing, and operations at 10pm, because nobody else in the building knows how.
>
> You don't need more leads sitting in a spreadsheet nobody calls. And you don't need another course collecting dust in a folder you already paid for.

**Hook Option 3: Direct financial loss, no scene, just the number**

> You spent four thousand dollars on ads this month. Maybe more. And somewhere between the lead and the chair, most of that money just disappeared.
>
> You don't need more leads sitting in a spreadsheet nobody calls. And you don't need another course collecting dust in a folder you already paid for.

---

## SHORTER VERSION (15 to 20 seconds, for retargeting or top of funnel testing)

> Two of today's leads never got a call back. One booked and never showed. By next week, they've probably found a med spa that called them back in ten minutes, not two days.
>
> You don't need more leads. You need a system that actually uses them.
>
> We bring the patients and hand you the exact playbook to convert them, built from twenty years running med spa operations.
>
> Click below for your Revenue Leak Audit.

---

## IMAGE AD COPY (static or carousel)

**Headline:** Three leads called back late. One never came in. That's this month's ad spend, gone.

**Body:** You've probably tried ads without follow up, or a course you paid for and never finished. The Luxora Collective brings the patients and hands you the exact playbook your staff needs to convert them, built from two decades of hands-on med spa experience.

**CTA:** Get your Revenue Leak Audit

---

## CASUAL SOCIAL CAPTION

> Paid for the course. Never finished module two. Meanwhile, your leads from this morning still haven't heard back from anyone 🤷🏼‍♀️
>
> The Luxora Collective brings the patients and hands you the exact system to actually convert them, built from two decades of real med spa experience, not another binder of theory.

---

## NOTE

All three hook options keep the rest of the script identical, so testing is clean: same diagnosis, same mechanism, same guarantee, only the opening 10 to 15 seconds changes. Worth running all three against each other before committing to one as primary, since scene-level pain (Option 1), identity pain (Option 2), and blunt financial loss (Option 3) will likely pull different segments of your audience.

content.text:
# Imagine — Visual Creation Suite ## Modules Call read_me again with the modules parameter to load detailed guidance: - `diagram` — SVG flowcharts, structural diagrams, illustrative diagrams - `mockup` — UI mockups, forms, cards, dashboards - `interactive` — interactive explainers with controls - `chart` — charts, data analysis, geographic maps (Chart.js, D3 choropleth) - `art` — illustration and generative art Pick the closest fit. The module includes all relevant design guidance. **Complexity budget — hard limits:** - Box subtitles: ≤5 words. Detail goes in click-through (`sendPrompt`) or the prose below — not the box. - Colors: ≤2 ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning (states, tiers), add a 1-line legend. Otherwise use one neutral ramp. - Horizontal tier: ≤4 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes → shrink to ≤110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail diagrams. If you catch yourself writing "click to learn more" in prose, the diagram itself must ACTUALLY be sparse. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything. **Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `

` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role="img"` with `` and `<desc>` instead — see SVG setup.) You create rich visual content — SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets — that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat. ## Core Design System These rules apply to ALL use cases. ### Philosophy - **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins. - **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces. - **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text. - **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** — All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks "explain X", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it. The user's font settings only apply to your response text, not to text inside the widget. ### Streaming Output streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early. - **HTML**: `<style>` (short) → content HTML → `<script>` last. - **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) → visual elements immediately. - Prefer inline `style="..."` over `<style>` blocks — inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream. - Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules — that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS. - Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead. ### Rules - No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming) - No font-size below 11px - No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class="ti ti-home"></i>`. Outline only — never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths. - No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects - No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only — host provides the bg) - **Typography**: The default font is Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `font-family: var(--font-voice)`. - **Headings**: h1 = 22px, h2 = 18px, h3 = 16px — all `font-weight: 500`. Heading color is pre-set to `var(--text-primary)` — don't override it. Body text = 16px, weight 400, `line-height: 1.7`. **Two weights only: 400 regular, 500 bold.** Never use 600 or 700 — they look heavy against the host UI. - **Sentence case** always. Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS. This applies everywhere including SVG text labels and diagram headings. - **No mid-sentence bolding**, including in your response text around the tool call. Entity names, class names, function names go in `code style` not **bold**. Bold is for headings and labels only. - The widget container is `display: block; width: 100%`. Your HTML fills it naturally — no wrapper div needed. Just start with your content directly. If you want vertical breathing room, add `padding: 1rem 0` on your first element. - Never use `position: fixed` — the iframe viewport sizes itself to your in-flow content height, so fixed-positioned elements (modals, overlays, tooltips) collapse it to `min-height: 100px`. For modal/overlay mockups: wrap everything in a normal-flow `<div style="min-height: 400px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.45); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;">` and put the modal inside — it's a faux viewport that actually contributes layout height. - No DOCTYPE, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` — just content fragments. - When placing text on a colored background (badges, pills, cards, tags), use the darkest shade from that same color family for the text — never plain black or generic gray. - **Corners**: use `border-radius: var(--radius)` for controls, `12px` for cards. In SVG, `rx="4"` is the default — larger values make pills, use only when you mean a pill. - **No rounded corners on single-sided borders** — if using `border-left` or `border-top` accents, set `border-radius: 0`. Rounded corners only work with full borders on all sides. - **No titles or prose inside the tool output** — see Philosophy above. - **Icon sizing**: Tabler `<i class="ti …">` sizes with `font-size` — 16–20px inline, 24px max decorative. For one-off inline SVG icons, set `width`/`height` explicitly (same limits). - No tabs, carousels, or `display: none` sections during streaming — hidden content streams invisibly. Show all content stacked vertically. (Post-streaming JS-driven steppers are fine — see Illustrative/Interactive sections.) - No nested scrolling — auto-fit height. - Scripts execute after streaming — load libraries via `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` (UMD globals), then use the global in a plain `<script>` that follows. The library `<script src>` tag must come BEFORE any inline script that uses its global — never call a library from code that appears above its `<script src>` tag. - **CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: external resources may ONLY load from `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com`, `fonts.googleapis.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com`. All other origins are blocked by the sandbox — the request silently fails. ### CSS Variables **Surfaces**: `--surface-2` (white), `--surface-1` (card), `--surface-0` (page bg); role tints `--bg-{accent,danger,success,warning}` **Text**: `--text-primary` (black), `--text-secondary` (muted), `--text-muted` (hints); role `--text-{accent,danger,success,warning}` **Borders**: `--border` (default hairline), `--border-strong` (hover), `--border-stronger`; role `--border-{accent,danger,success,warning}` **Typography**: `--font-sans`, `--font-voice` (serif), `--font-mono` **Layout**: `--radius` (8px), `--pad-{sm,md,lg,xl}`, `--gap-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}`; for larger corners use literal `12px`/`16px` All auto-adapt to light/dark mode. For custom colors in HTML, use CSS variables. **Dark mode is mandatory** — every color must work in both modes: - In SVG: use the pre-built color classes (`c-blue`, `c-teal`, `c-amber`, etc.) for colored nodes — they handle light/dark mode automatically. Never write `<style>` blocks for colors. - In SVG: every `<text>` element needs a class (`t`, `ts`, `th`) — never omit fill or use `fill="inherit"`. Inside a `c-{color}` parent, text classes auto-adjust to the ramp. - In HTML: always use CSS variables (--text-primary, --text-secondary) for text. Never hardcode colors like color: #333 — invisible in dark mode. - Mental test: if the background were near-black, would every text element still be readable? ### sendPrompt(text) A global function that sends a message to chat as if the user typed it. Use it when the user's next step benefits from Claude thinking. Handle filtering, sorting, toggling, and calculations in JS instead. ### Links `<a href="https://...">` just works — clicks are intercepted and open the host's link-confirmation dialog. Or call `openLink(url)` directly. ## When nothing fits Pick the closest use case below and adapt. When nothing fits cleanly: - Default to editorial layout if the content is explanatory - Default to card layout if the content is a bounded object - All core design system rules still apply - Use `sendPrompt()` for any action that benefits from Claude thinking ## SVG setup **ViewBox safety checklist** — before finalizing any SVG, verify: 1. Find your lowest element: max(y + height) across all rects, max(y) across all text baselines. 2. Set viewBox height = that value + 40px buffer. 3. Find your rightmost element: max(x + width) across all rects. All content must stay within x=0 to x=680. 4. For text with text-anchor="end", the text extends LEFT from x. If x=118 and text is 200px wide, it starts at x=-82 — outside the viewBox. Increase x or use text-anchor="start". 5. Never use negative x or y coordinates. The viewBox starts at 0,0. 6. **No unintentional overlaps.** For every pair of elements that aren't meant to layer (label-on-label, label-on-arrow, box-on-box, callout-on-shape), check their bounding boxes do not intersect. The only allowed overlaps are deliberate: a label centered inside its own box, an arrowhead touching the box it points to, a highlight rect behind the thing it highlights. If two unrelated elements would collide, move one — shorten the label, shift the y, add a row. A diagram with crossed labels reads as broken regardless of how good the content is. 7. Flowcharts/structural only: for every pair of boxes in the same row, check that the left box's (x + width) is less than the right box's x by at least 20px. If four 160px boxes plus three 20px gaps sum to more than 640px, the row doesn't fit — shrink the boxes or cut the subtitles, don't let them overlap. **SVG setup**: `<svg width="100%" viewBox="0 0 680 H" role="img"><title>………` — 680px wide, flexible height.
